title: Technology Sector Update for 07/12/2018: CA,AVGO,LEDS,I,CSCO

Tech stocks were outpacing all other sectors Thursday, with shares of technology companies in the S&P 500 adding more than 1.4% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was climbing over 0.5% in afternoon trading.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) dropped over 3% Thursday afternoon, paring a more than 7% mid-morning decline, that followed new regulatory filings showing activist investor Starboard Value LP reducing its stake in the chipmaker to 8.6% from 10.5% previously. Starboard said the stock sales reflect the need to rebalance its portfolio following the significant appreciation in Mellanox' share price since the hedge fund first acquired its stock in November 2017.
In other sector news:
+ CA Technologies ( CA ) raced nearly 19% higher on Thursday, at one point peaking at $44.00 a share to reach its best share price since the dot-com boom peaked in March 2000, when the software and applications company agreed to an $18.9 billion takeover offer from Broadcom ( AVGO ). Under terms of the proposed transaction, CA investors will receive $44.50 in cash for each of their shares, representing a 19.6% premium over Wednesday's closing price. Broadcom is expecting the deal to immediately add to its non-GAAP per-share earnings after closing, which is expected before the end of the year, pending shareholder and anti-trust approvals by regulators in the United States, the European Union and Japan. Its shares were down almost 15% in recent trading.
+ Intelsat SA ( I ) was orbiting more than 10% higher on Thursday, easing slightly from a nearly 14% gain earlier that followed it announcing an agreement with fellow satellite operators SES SA and Eutelsat on the use of lower C-band satellite spectrum in the United States. The proposal was initiated by Intelsat, together with Intel ( INTC ) and SES, in response to proceedings by the Federal Communications Commission. The new pact establishes a commercial and technical framework and enables terrestrial mobile operators to quickly access spectrum in the 3,700 to 4,200 megahertz frequency band in the United States and supports the accelerated deployment of 5G networks by mobile operators.
- SemiLEDs (LEDS) Thursday was trading just over 9% lower in recent trading, staying about 1.0 percentage points above its session low, despite late Wednesday reporting improved fiscal Q3 financial results over the same quarter last year. The light-emitting diode chips and components manufacturer slashed its GAAP net loss by almost 72% compared with year-ago levels, posting a $0.09 per share net loss during the three months ended May 31 after recording a net loss of $0.32 per share during the March-to-May reporting period last year. Revenue grew 30% over year-ago levels to $2 million. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison.
